skill.name: ddd-tactical-patterns
skill.description: Apply DDD tactical patterns in code using entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, and domain events with explicit invariants.
skill.summary: Turn domain rules into explicit, behavior-rich models with clear invariants and aggregate boundaries.
skill.author: sickn33

content.user_title: Design Domain Models with DDD Tactical Patterns
content.value_statement: Domain rules often become scattered across controllers and persistence code. This skill structures them with aggregates, value objects, repositories, and domain events.
actual_capabilities: Identifies invariants before defining aggregate boundaries.
Models validated concepts as immutable value objects.
Places domain behavior inside entities and aggregate roots.
Defines repository contracts around aggregate roots.
Uses domain events for meaningful state transitions.
Reviews designs with a focused tactical pattern checklist.
limitations: Does not define bounded contexts or other strategic DDD boundaries.
Does not select databases, transport protocols, or deployment architecture.
Does not replace tests for aggregate invariants and event behavior.
May introduce unnecessary complexity for simple data-oriented applications.

use_cases.title: Model a New Business Workflow
use_cases.description: Translate workflow rules into aggregates, value objects, methods, and domain events.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers starting a domain-focused feature

use_cases.title: Refactor an Anemic Domain Model
use_cases.description: Move business rules from controllers and services into behavior-rich domain objects.
use_cases.target_user: Senior engineers improving an existing codebase

use_cases.title: Review Tactical DDD Boundaries
use_cases.description: Assess aggregate consistency, repository scope, value semantics, and event payload design.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Core Invariants
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this business rule set: [rules]. List the invariants, affected concepts, and state transitions before proposing any classes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a small domain workflow

prompt_templates.title: Design an Aggregate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an aggregate for [workflow]. Define its root, entities, value objects, invariants, commands, and meaningful domain events.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Domain Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this model: [model description]. Find anemic behavior, misplaced rules, persistence leakage, and weak boundaries. Propose a focused tactical DDD refactor.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing design

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Cross-Aggregate Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these aggregates and transaction requirements: [details]. Separate immediate invariants from eventual consistency. Recommend repository and domain event boundaries with tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Model order submission where an order must contain items and may be submitted once.
output_examples.output: Aggregate root: Order. Invariants: at least one item and draft status. Transition: submit. Event: OrderSubmitted.

output_examples.input: Review a service that validates money values and directly saves ORM records.
output_examples.output: Introduce an immutable Money value object. Move validation into construction. Define a repository interface that persists aggregate roots without exposing ORM entities.

output_examples.input: Choose consistency boundaries for inventory reservation and payment authorization.
output_examples.output: Keep each capability in its own aggregate. Publish stable domain events and coordinate eventual consistency outside both aggregate roots.

best_practices: State invariants explicitly before selecting entities or aggregate boundaries.
Keep transactions within one aggregate whenever business rules permit.
Pair each modeled invariant with focused automated tests.
anti_patterns: Do not place core business rules only in controllers or application services.
Do not expose persistence models as domain entities.
Do not require synchronous consistency across unrelated aggregates without a proven invariant.

faq.question: What tactical patterns does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, domain events, and explicit invariant enforcement.

faq.question: Does this skill define bounded contexts?
faq.answer: No. Establish strategic boundaries before applying these tactical patterns.

faq.question: Can it choose a database or ORM?
faq.answer: No. It keeps domain design separate from database and ORM selection.

faq.question: When should I avoid full DDD?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the domain is simple and tactical abstractions add more complexity than value.

faq.question: How should repositories be scoped?
faq.answer: Define repositories around aggregate roots and expose operations in domain language.

faq.question: How should domain events be designed?
faq.answer: Use past-tense names, minimal stable payloads, and versioned schemas for breaking changes.
